description: F129 (Sprint 51): Review No Rule Items screen -- filter chips and the covered-item sweep's reload path. COVERS the Sprint 50 surfaces MT-3 (the screen is reachable -- post-F135 it IS the home screen when accounts exist, so reachability is proven by its chips resolving on launch, not by an entry-point click) and MT-2c (sweep runs on every load). READ-ONLY: clicks filter chips and navigates only -- creates no rules, adds no safe senders, marks nothing processed -- so it is inherently net-zero on the dev DB; the final steps return to the home screen. TWO HARNESS CONSTRAINTS drove this design (Sprint 51 discovery, both re-confirmed live): (1) `ww_assert*` is NOT replayable by the script runner (README line 195) -- a case containing only asserts reports FAILED even when the UI is correct, so verification here is expressed as CLICKS: a click that resolves proves the element exists with that exact name, and a missing element errors the step. (2) The Windows UIA projection of Flutter semantics surfaces only widgets carrying a `tooltip:` plus screen titles and Text nodes; `Semantics(label:)` on a merged container does NOT project, so account ROWS are unaddressable by name and are deliberately not used. SELECTORS VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-28 against dev build 0.5.8; REWORKED 2026-08-15 (Sprint 59): F135 (Sprint 52) made this screen the app default -- the home-screen entry-point click and 'Back' teardown steps were structurally stale (the screen has no self-referential icon and no Back; it is the root) and the reload tooltip was renamed from 'Refresh' to 'Re-check the last scan (does not fetch new mail)' per Harold's Sprint 52 feedback. Screen-name renamed to 'Review No Rule Items' per F155.

testCases.title: Post-F135 home screen renders filter chips; reload re-runs the sweep; navigation round-trip survives

steps._comment: PRIMING QUERY -- also guarantees a maximized window so nothing is off-screen.

MT-3 (post-F135 form): the app opens ON the Review No Rule Items screen when accounts exist. The 'All Accounts' chip exists only on this screen, so it resolving IS the reachability proof. MT-2c evidence: the count chips carry the post-sweep totals -- counts are data-dependent, prefix match keeps the script valid across scans.

MT-2c: the reload button re-enters _loadItems, which runs the covered-item sweep before display. The screen must survive the reload with its chips intact. Tooltip renamed from 'Refresh' in Sprint 52 (Harold: 'Refresh' read as 'go check for new mail', which this does not do).
steps.selector: type=Button[name='Re-check the last scan (does not fetch new mail)']

steps._comment: Navigation round-trip: away to Scan History and Back. Post-F135 there is no 'Back' FROM this screen (it is the root; the X is Exit Application) -- teardown is simply being back on it, proven by the chip resolving again.
